subject: Multi-nodal recovery window exception request — Veridian Systems
messages:
From: Alex Morton <alex.morton@veridiansystems.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@veridiansystems.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: multi-nodal recovery window exception for Veridian deployment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We finished our internal readiness run and have one request before we sign the Dedicated contract for APAC: a temporary exception to the standard 15-minute warm-standby activation SLA.

Context: Veridian's production topology in APAC spans three sovereign nodes (two active, one standby) with cross-region replication handled by a third-party WAN accelerator. During our last live failover test the warm-standby required ~28 minutes to fully catch up due to checksum reconciliation at the WAN layer — most of that time is outside Redwood's runtime but affects our RTO targets.

What we're asking: a carveout for the first 12 months post-migration that sets a 30-minute RTO for APAC failovers (instead of 15m), tied to a runbook and additional telemetry that both teams operate. We want this limited exception to be explicitly scoped to the APAC deployment and to be removed after a jointly agreed remediation plan (software patch + WAN config change) is validated in production canaries.

We've attached replication metrics from the last run and a proposed runbook. Happy to discuss trade-offs on credits or extended support windows.

Best,
Alex
Alex Morton
Director, Infrastructure — Veridian Systems
+61 2 9876 5432
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morton <alex.morton@veridiansystems.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-nodal recovery window exception for Veridian deployment

Alex — thanks for the detailed note and attached data. I copied Kimberly (SRE) and Naomi (Legal/compliance) so we can address operational and contractual side.

Quick reactions:
- We want to avoid open-ended SLA exceptions, but a 12-month scoped exception tied to observable remediation and canary gates is reasonable.
- From the platform side we can commit to:
  * extra telemetry surface (per-request activation timestamps, KV-cache warmup metrics)
  * a daily ingestion of your WAN checksum/replay metrics into our incident dashboard during the remediation period
  * a canary plan that validates reduced activation time before the exception sunset
- Commercially: we can offer a limited service credit cap (0.5% monthly revenue for APAC tier) for missed SLA during the exception window in lieu of full SLA exposure.

Kimberly / Naomi — can you weigh in on the operational checklist and contractual language to scope this to APAC and the 12-month remediation milestone? Kim, can we also run a focused load/activation test with Veridian next Wednesday?

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
On Tue, 20 Mar 2028 at 09:14 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi all — I dug into the runbook and metrics. A few notes: 
> 
> 1) The observed 28-minute tail is dominated by external WAN reconciliation (see attached CSV), which our runtime can't expedite but can better pipeline during failover.
> 2) Operational mitigation we can deploy immediately: staged KV prefetch, parallel replay workers, and a short pre-failover quiesce that reduces reconciliation divergence. We estimate these measures will reduce activation time to ~18–20m in most runs.
> 3) To reach the 15m SLO we'll need the WAN vendor to eliminate a per-chunk checksum step; we can validate that in a controlled canary once they have a patch.
> 
> Proposed plan (operations):
> - Short-term (0–30 days): enable KV prefetch + parallel replay on your APAC cluster (no code change, config-only), schedule a full activation test next Wed 03/22.
> - Medium-term (30–120 days): coordinate with WAN vendor for checksum patch; we'll run iterative canaries.
> - Exception: 30-minute RTO for APAC for 12 months starting 03/24/2028, automatically removing once canary metrics meet the 15m gate for 3 consecutive successful runbooks.
> 
> I'll run the activation test with Veridian engineers next Wednesday. Attaching a test checklist.
> 
> Kim
> Kimberly Park
> Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morton <alex.morton@veridiansystems.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 12:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-nodal recovery window exception for Veridian deployment

Alex / team — legal reviewed the ask. Key contractual bullets we'll need in the amendment: 
- Scope: explicit APAC-only carveout; all other regions remain under standard SLA.
- Term: 12 months with conditional early termination (automatic) if runbook canaries meet 15m gate for three consecutive successful activations.
- Telemetry: Redwood will ingest and retain Veridian's replication telemetry for the remediation period; both parties have access for verification.
- Compensation: agreed credit cap of 0.5% monthly APAC revenue for missed SLA during the exception window; exceptions outside of this must go through executive approval.
- Security: Veridian must grant read-only logs to our SOC for the remediation period to ensure there are no data integrity issues during replay.

Marissa — can your contracts team convert this into a redline? I'd like to get a draft to Veridian by EOD Thurs so we can keep their migration schedule.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morton <alex.morton@veridiansystems.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-nodal recovery window exception for Veridian deployment

Karthik / Naomi / Kim / Marissa — thanks, this is all reasonable. We consent to the APAC-only, 12-month scoped exception, the telemetry sharing, and the 0.5% monthly credit cap. We'll schedule the activation test for Wed 03/22 and share live metrics. Please send the redline and we'll push the WAN vendor (AuroraLink) for the checksum patch timeline.

Next steps agreed:
- Redwood to enable KV prefetch + parallel replay on 03/21 (ops change)
- Activation test on 03/22 with both teams; Veridian will upload replication metrics to the shared drive immediately after the test
- Marissa to share contract redline by EOD 03/23 for Veridian review

Appreciate the fast turn — Alex

--
Alex Morton
Director, Infrastructure — Veridian Systems
